label: Prosser v. PharmaLogic Holdings — a $200,000 EBITDA shortfall against a $6.6m cliff
provenance: PUBLIC RECORD. Prosser v. PharmaLogic Holdings Corp., C.A. No. N25C-08-284 MAA CCLD (Del. Super. Ct., Complex Commercial Litigation Division, July 7, 2026), as summarised at delawarechancery.foxrothschild.com. Figures below are the ones the source states: a $7,000,000 EBITDA threshold, a $6,600,000 payment for EBITDA between $7,000,000 and $7,499,999, and a buyer-reported EBITDA of $6,800,000 — $200,000 short. Nothing here is invented, and nothing is added where the source is silent.
simplifications: The real clause is tiered above $7,499,999. This file expresses only the tier that was in play, because that is the tier the dispute turned on. A tiered clause as a whole is not expressible in the signed terms — see case-winshall-viacom.json for the same refusal.

oneOffOutflows carries only the one adjustment a source quantifies: 'more than $170,000 in additional expenses from switching to a new supplier' (Fox Rothschild summary). A second source (Reed Smith) attributes no dollar amount to any individual action, so this figure rests on one source. The other alleged items — higher bad debt, a new 401(k) match, sales bonuses — have no published figures and are not in this file.

The sources give no length for the earnout period, so it is expressed as a single period measured once. If the real clause measured several periods, this file is the right arithmetic on the wrong shape.

deal.metricName: Earnout period EBITDA (as defined in the purchase agreement)

schedule.basisHash: n/a — the public record has no account snapshot to hash

settled.note: No earnout was paid. The buyer's earnout statement reported $6,800,000 against a $7,000,000 threshold. The sellers' claim that buyer-side charges depressed the figure survived dismissal in part and is live litigation, so the settled figure here is what was actually paid, not what a court may later order.
